# BorderDay

> BorderDay is an employer-first record-keeping and reminder tool for cross-border day counting. HR and employees track telework, on-site, trip and non-working days. Social-security telework counters run on all nine border routes; tax counters run on seven. HR sees day types per date, night-away marks and counts, never GPS or device location.

- Site: https://borderday.com
- Languages: English, French, German, Italian, Dutch
- Routes covered: Geneva and other non-1983 cantons←France (tax and social security), 1983-agreement cantons←France (tax and social security), Germany→Switzerland (tax and social security), France→Luxembourg (tax and social security), Belgium→Luxembourg (tax and social security), Germany→Luxembourg (tax and social security), Italy→Switzerland (tax and social security), France→Belgium (social security; no day limit for tax), Netherlands→Belgium (social security; no tax tolerance found).
- Border routes covered (v1): nine, in five regions (Geneva, Basel, Ticino, Luxembourg, Belgium)
- Social-security counters: all nine border routes (EU/EEA/CH framework: under 25%, 25% to under 50% with A1, 50% or more)
- Tax counters running: Geneva and other non-1983 cantons←France (40% / 10 mission days), 1983-agreement cantons←France (40% / 10 mission days / 45 overnight stays away from the residence state: at most one Swiss night per working week; occasional third-country business trips count; part-time pro rata rounded down; part-year 20% of working days; extra third-state mission days beyond the 10 and the 40% also count; taxed in France), Germany→Switzerland (60 non-return days + 20% regular return; part-year 5×months+1×weeks; part-time base 240/280), France→Luxembourg (34 days, reduced for part-time), Belgium→Luxembourg (34 days, not reduced for part-time), Germany→Luxembourg (34 days, not reduced for part-time), Italy→Switzerland (25% / 45 non-return days)
- No general tax counter: France→Belgium (no day limit), Netherlands→Belgium (no tolerance found). Do not describe BorderDay as tracking tax limits on these border routes.
- Day log: the free preview stays on the device; with a plan or company account it is saved to the account. No GPS or device location.
- Company accounts: invite by email, HR dashboard with the same counters employees see
- Not tax advice, legal advice, or a substitute for your employer, a qualified tax adviser, or the competent social-security institution
- Thresholds shown are taken from public official sources and may change; where a rule cannot be counted, no number is shown and users are pointed to their authority
- Subscriptions: individuals €4.99/month or €49/year (incl. VAT); companies €5/active employee/month (min €39/month, excl. VAT); yearly company minimum €390, excl. VAT (2 months free). 7-day free trial, then the plan chosen at the stated price, charged automatically on day 8 and renewing until cancelled; card required at signup. Checkout via Stripe Managed Payments (sold through Link).
- Contact: hello@borderday.com

- https://borderday.com/en/guides/ — English only, no translated version: guide hub for the France-resident Geneva and Luxembourg day-count guides, and how employers track those days
- https://borderday.com/en/guides/france-geneva-telework-days/ — English only, no translated version: how a France resident employed in Geneva counts telework and temporary missions
- Short answer (Geneva): If you live in France and work for an employer in Geneva, telework from France stays taxable in Switzerland up to 40% of your annual working time in a calendar year. That 40% can include up to 10 days of temporary missions in France or another country. Above 40%, the pay for your telework days becomes taxable in France from the first telework day, not just the excess.
- https://borderday.com/en/guides/france-luxembourg-telework-days/ — English only, no translated version: how a France resident employed in Luxembourg counts telework days
- Short answer (Luxembourg): If you are tax resident in France and employed in Luxembourg, you can spend up to 34 days per tax year physically working in France or a third country and your whole salary stays taxable in Luxembourg. Any part of a day counts as a full day, and part-time or part-year work reduces the 34 in proportion. Above 34 days, France can tax the pay for the time you actually worked outside Luxembourg, from the first day.
- https://borderday.com/en/guides/how-to-track-cross-border-telework-days/ — English only, no translated version: how employers can keep a day-by-day record of cross-border telework
- Short answer (tracking): Employers of cross-border staff need a day-by-day record of where and how each employee worked, because tax and social security rules each use their own count. In Switzerland, employers of France residents (outside the 1983 cross-border agreement) must track telework and mission days actually worked and report an annual rate, even when it is 0%. In Luxembourg, every telework arrangement of a non-resident employee must be declared to social security.
- https://borderday.com/fr/guides/ — French only, no translated version: guide hub for the France-resident guides (Luxembourg, Geneva, Basel)
- https://borderday.com/fr/guides/france-luxembourg-compter-jours-teletravail/ — French only, no translated version: how a France resident employed in Luxembourg counts telework days
- En bref (France–Luxembourg): si vous résidez fiscalement en France et êtes employé au Luxembourg, le télétravail et les jours travaillés hors du Luxembourg ne relèvent pas d’un seul plafond. Le seuil fiscal publié est de 34 jours par période imposable passés physiquement en France et/ou dans un État tiers pour y exercer l’emploi. La sécurité sociale suit un autre compteur, en pourcentage du temps de travail, avec un accord-cadre possible entre 25 % et moins de 50 %. Ces deux seuils ne se compensent pas. Un tableur, un calendrier ou un export n’est pas, à lui seul, une preuve de votre présence physique.
- https://borderday.com/fr/guides/france-geneve-compter-jours-teletravail/ — French only, no translated version: how a France resident employed in Geneva counts telework and temporary missions
- En bref (Genève): pour un salarié résidant en France et travaillant à Genève, le télétravail effectué en France peut rester imposé en Suisse jusqu’à 40 % du temps d’activité par année civile. Depuis le 1er janvier 2026, cette règle relève de l’avenant à la convention fiscale franco-suisse, avec un suivi des jours par l’employeur. Cette limite inclut jusqu’à 10 jours de missions temporaires en France ou dans un État tiers. Au-delà de 40 %, la part de salaire liée au télétravail est imposable en France dès le premier jour de télétravail, et non seulement pour l’excédent. La sécurité sociale est un autre compteur, en pourcentage du temps de travail (accord-cadre possible entre 25 % et moins de 50 %). Ces règles genevoises de suivi ne doivent pas être transposées telles quelles à toute la Suisse, ni au régime frontalier de 1983 applicable dans d’autres cantons.
- https://borderday.com/fr/guides/france-bale-compter-jours-teletravail/ — French only, no translated version: how a France resident employed in Basel under the 1983 agreement counts telework, missions and overnight stays
- En bref (Bâle): si vous résidez en France et travaillez pour un employeur établi à Bâle-Ville ou à Bâle-Campagne, votre salaire relève en principe de l’accord frontalier franco-suisse du 11 avril 1983 : il est imposé en France, et la Suisse reçoit de la France une compensation de 4,5 % de la masse salariale brute. Pour garder ce régime, trois limites se suivent en parallèle : le télétravail en France jusqu’à 40 % du temps de travail par année civile, dont au plus 10 jours de missions temporaires en France ou dans un État tiers, et au plus 45 nuitées par an hors de l’État de résidence, avec des règles précises de décompte. La sécurité sociale est un autre compteur, en pourcentage du temps de travail (accord-cadre possible entre 25 % et moins de 50 %). Ces règles ne valent ni pour Genève, ni pour Zurich, ni pour toute la Suisse.
- https://borderday.com/de/guides/ — German only, no translated version: guide hub for the Germany–Switzerland day-count guide
- https://borderday.com/de/guides/deutschland-schweiz-grenzgaenger-tage-zaehlen/ — German only, no translated version: how a Germany resident working in Switzerland counts non-return days, commute days and home office
- Kurz gesagt (Deutschland–Schweiz): Wer in Deutschland wohnt, in der Schweiz arbeitet und regelmässig nach Hause zurückkehrt, ist Grenzgängerin oder Grenzgänger nach Art. 15a des Doppelbesteuerungsabkommens (DBA) Deutschland-Schweiz. Die Schweiz darf dann höchstens 4,5 % des Bruttolohns an der Quelle erheben, Deutschland besteuert den Lohn und rechnet diese Steuer an. Seit dem 1. Januar 2026 gelten zwei Zähler nebeneinander: höchstens 60 Nichtrückkehrtage im Jahr, und mindestens 20 % der vereinbarten Arbeitstage mit Pendeln an den Arbeitsort. Volle Homeoffice-Tage sind weder Nichtrückkehrtage noch Pendeltage. Die Regel gilt für alle Kantone, nicht nur für Basel. Die Sozialversicherung folgt einem anderen Zähler, in Prozent der Arbeitszeit.
- https://borderday.com/it/guides/ — Italian only, no translated version: guide hub for the Italy–Ticino day-count guide
- https://borderday.com/it/guides/italia-ticino-contare-giorni-telelavoro/ — Italian only, no translated version: how an Italy resident working in Ticino counts telework and non-return days
- In breve (Italia–Ticino): per chi abita in Italia in un Comune della fascia di 20 km dal confine e lavora come dipendente nell’area di frontiera svizzera (Ticino, Grigioni o Vallese), l’Accordo italo-svizzero sui frontalieri del 23 dicembre 2020 fissa due limiti per anno civile senza cambiare lo status di frontaliere: al massimo il 25 % dell’attività in telelavoro presso il proprio domicilio in Italia, e al massimo 45 giorni di mancato rientro quotidiano per motivi professionali, esclusi ferie e malattia. Il Protocollo di modifica che fissa queste regole è in vigore dal 9 febbraio 2026 e si applica dal 1° gennaio 2024. La sicurezza sociale segue un altro contatore, in percentuale del tempo di lavoro.
